leads.posting: Chapter Homes Bags ₹63 Cr To Build Home & Kitchen Tech Brands. Omnichannel furniture and home furnishings brand Chapter Homes has raised ₹63 Cr ($6.6 Mn) in a strategic funding round through a mix of debt and equity. The fundraise valued the startup at nearly ₹1,000 Cr (around $106 Mn). The round saw participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, comedian Tanmay Bhat and a clutch of family offices. The brand claims to have also received further commitments from undisclosed backers for a future fundraise. In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to strengthen product development, expand into newer categories and invest in technology and brand building. A chunk of the capital will also be used to scale its omnichannel distribution network and set up its initial offline footprint. “… Consumers are increasingly looking for better-designed products, trusted quality, strong functionality and a superior overall experience – online and in store – and we see a meaningful opportunity to build for those needs. That is why we are building focused brands for each category across home and kitchen,” said Chapter Homes cofounder Nitin Chugh. Founded in 2025 by former PharmEasy executives Chugh, Akarsh Bharadwaj, Shrey Mittal, Dhiraj Jain and Dheeraj Goyal, Chapter Homes claims to be building multiple consumer brands across categories for home and kitchen needs of Indian consumers. It has already launched a home furnishing brand under HOKIPO. Going forward, it plans to leverage synergies across supply chain, content, technology and distribution to expand into adjacent categories such as cookware, home décor and small kitchen appliances. The startup also said that it plans to leverage AI across cataloguing and demand forecasting to product assortment and customer retention to launch faster and rein in costs. leads.posting: Construction robotics startup Origin raises $20 Mn led by Accel, Zacua Ventures. Origin, a physical AI startup building robots for interior construction, has raised $20 million in total funding in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21, along with angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla. The company will use the funds to expand its robot fleet, deploy its flagship robot OG-1 and conduct customer pilots in the US and Europe. It also plans to expand its robotics platform to additional interior construction tasks. Founded in 2025 by Yogesh Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin develops robots designed to automate interior construction work. Its flagship robot, OG-1, currently handles wall finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding and priming walls. The robot is designed to operate across commercial spaces, residential apartments, data centres, hotels and warehouses. The company said it deployed its first robots at construction sites in New York within 10 months of its founding. Origin is preparing for pilots with customers in the US and Europe, including two large drywall finishing contractors in the US. It also plans to conduct pilots in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia. The startup's robots are powered by its Construction Action Model, a foundation model developed for construction workflows. The system combines task planning, autonomous navigation and tool control to help robots perform construction tasks and adapt to changing site conditions. Origin plans to expand OG-1's capabilities to tasks such as taping, drywall installation, drilling and conduit installation. The company is targeting the deployment of 150 robots by the end of 2027. The funding comes amid rising interest in construction robotics as companies look to address labour shortages and improve productivity. AI startup RapidCanvas has raised $29 million in a Series B funding round led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India, with participation from Hitachi Ventures and existing investors Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures. The latest round takes the company’s total funding to $52.5 million. The company will use the proceeds to expand its go to market teams, strengthen partnerships and grow its field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil. Founded in 2021, RapidCanvas provides an AI platform that combines AI agents with human expertise to help enterprises build and deploy custom AI applications. Its platform aims to help businesses move AI projects from pilots to production. The company said its annual recurring revenue grew 8x over the past six quarters. More than 40% of its customers now run multiple AI use cases in production. In 2026, over 75 enterprises across manufacturing, financial services, retail, business services and infrastructure made 1.4 million AI led decisions using applications built on its platform. RapidCanvas offers three core products: Enterprise Context Engine, Visual Development Canvas and Operational Harness. These products help enterprises capture business context, develop custom AI applications and manage deployed AI solutions. The company targets enterprises with annual revenue of $100 million to $10 billion that have AI budgets but lack the resources or expertise to deploy custom AI applications. Its model combines an AI platform with field engineers who work with customers to build applications and oversee their outcomes after deployment. In December 2024, RapidCanvas raised $16 million in a Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Titanium Ventures, Accel and Valley Capital Partners.
